title: Extend FirestorePermissionDeniedException conversion beyond the 2 read call sites it currently covers
rule: Nygard lens (mandatory for this area) — permission-denied at every I/O point; EH-2 typed-exception boundary

evidence.quote: Thrown when a Firestore operation returns PERMISSION_DENIED.

why: _guardPermission (firestore_gateway_impl.dart:1197-1215) is the ONLY code in the app that ever throws FirestorePermissionDeniedException, and it wraps exactly 2 of this gateway's ~30 Firestore I/O methods — fetchPage (524) and fetchChildPage (1051), both reads, both with operation hardcoded to 'read'. None of the ~23 push* (write) methods route through it: pushStreak/pushSettings/pushTrack (288-337) issue raw .set() calls with no try/catch at all, and pushCompletionsBatch (246-285) wraps any commit failure — including permission-denied — as a generic SyncPushException instead. Traced end to end: OutboxProcessor absorbs every push failure internally (never rethrows to any AsyncValue/UI, so this is not a UI-facing bug), but the dedicated permission_denied analytics event in sync_orchestrator.dart (gated on `e is FirestorePermissionDeniedException`) therefore fires only from the pull path and never from an outbox push. The write path's only detector of this failure class is outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters, which pattern-matches raw persisted error text (`lastError.like('%permission-denied%')`) instead of a structured type — a duplicated, Firestore-SDK-wording-dependent re-derivation of the exact fact this exception exists to represent. This repo's own docs (on-device-preflight-cheatsheet.md, bug-hunt-findings-2026-05-31.md) call permission-denied on writes 'a known recurring failure mode in this project,' yet the typed signal for it covers roughly 1 in 15 of the gateway's I/O surface.
recommendation: Route every push*/fetch* method in firestore_gateway_impl.dart through _guardPermission (or an equivalent shared wrapper) with an accurate operation value (read/write/delete) instead of only the 2 fetch methods, so FirestorePermissionDeniedException becomes the single source of truth for 'this failure was permission-denied' on both read and write paths. Then simplify outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters to check a structured signal instead of a LIKE-pattern on free text.
acceptance_criteria: count of _guardPermission( call sites in firestore_gateway_impl.dart increases beyond the current 2 to cover write (push*) methods

a new test asserts a push method (e.g. pushCompletionsBatch) surfaces FirestorePermissionDeniedException — not a generic SyncPushException/raw FirebaseException — when the underlying commit fails with code permission-denied
a test shows sync_orchestrator's permission_denied analytics event firing from a simulated outbox push failure, not only from pullOnLaunch
